newsitem.title: CANADA: Marketing, transmission boost TCPL results.
newsitem.headline: Marketing, transmission boost TCPL results.

text.p: TransCanada PipeLines Ltd, which earlier on Friday reported higher 1996 earnings and revenues, said strong performance from its energy transmission and marketing businesses bolstered results.
TransCanada said net earnings from its energy transmission segement were C$323.6 million in 1996, up C$17.3 million from the year before.
The company's Canadian natural gas mainline contributed C$250.7 million to the division's earnings, down from C$253.6 million in 1995.
TransCanada said increases from the mainline's incentive regulation partially offset a one percent drop in its allowed rate of return on common equity.
The company's share of earnings from other North American pipeline investments rose C$20.2 million from the previous year to C$72.9 million, it said.
The energy marketing segment posted net earnings of C$27.9 million in 1996, up C$17.6 million from the year before, the company said.
TransCanada said the increase came as a result of higher prices and volumes of natural gas, new market ventures and strong margins for refined products.

Energy processing earnings in 1996 rose to C$41.6 million from C$32.1 million in 1995, with much of the increase coming from higher ownership in gathering and processing as well as specialty chemicals businesses acquired with the remaining shares of Alberta Natural Gas Ltd in March, it said.

TransCanada's international division posted a net loss of C$5.2 million, a C$7.9 million improvement as a result of lower project costs and income contributions from the Cusiana pipeline in Colombia in 1996.
The company said its natural gas mainline delivered 2.44 trillion cubic feet of gas in 1996, up from 2.35 TCF in 1995.
The total included 1.27 TCF delivered to domestic customers and 1.17 TCF to customers serving U.S. markets.
